steps.label: Prompt
steps.text:
Make a 33-second launch film for [your product], 16:9 at 1920x1080, from the "13-self-planning-calendar" template in lumian2015/opus-5-5-video-templates (MIT, rendered with HyperFrames).

Setup: clone https://github.com/lumian2015/opus-5-5-video-templates into ~/.claude/skills/opus-5-5-video-templates, then run `npx hyperframes@0.8.96 doctor` and fix anything it reports (it needs Node.js 22 or newer, FFmpeg and Chrome).

The film, scene by scene:
1. the frame is one red dot; it shrinks, draws the now-line, and a calendar grid grows out of it
2. meetings fly in and pile up; the hook headline blurs in, then everything collapses into the dot
3. dark lockup: two blocks and the now-dot assemble into the mark, wordmark and tagline slide out
4. the top block opens into the app window; the week fills with events and the clash badge counts them
5. camera pushes onto the prompt bar; the prompt is typed with live-highlighted chips; the send button floods the screen
6. the red collapses into a tilted now-line; the week reshuffles in 3D, protected blocks drop in, clashes count down to none
7. three split-screen close-ups: a meeting slides to a free slot, a morning block refuses an invite, an overrun pushes the afternoon down
8. the week becomes one tile among hundreds; the field tilts, blurs, and the dot lands as the period of the end line
9. the end line turns into blocks that fold into the mark; lockup with domain; everything shrinks back to the dot

Before you change anything, learn [your product] from [your product URL] and ask me only for what you cannot find: its name, what it does in one line, the copy each scene needs, and two or three brand colours as #rrggbb. The demo brand, names, prices, numbers, ratings and quotes are placeholders: replace every one with something true for my product, or remove it. Never ship a made-up number or testimonial.

Then:
1. `node ~/.claude/skills/opus-5-5-video-templates/scripts/new-video.mjs 13-self-planning-calendar my-video`
2. `node ~/.claude/skills/opus-5-5-video-templates/scripts/vars.mjs my-video` to list the variables.
3. Write values.json, keeping each value close to its default's length and format (the same number of |-separated items, plain numbers where the default is a number), then apply it with `node ~/.claude/skills/opus-5-5-video-templates/scripts/vars.mjs my-video values.json`.
4. `cd my-video && npx hyperframes@0.8.96 snapshot --at 1,11,22,32`, look at every frame, and fix any text that overflows or any colour that is hard to read.
5. `npx hyperframes@0.8.96 render -f 60 -q high -w 4 -o out.mp4`, then watch it through once before you hand it over.

Template notes: Square brackets in the prompt mark the phrases that turn into chips once typed. Feature captions take | as a line break. The week itself (titles, times, clashes, what moves where) lives in the EV array: each row has a messy slot, a planned slot (or null when it moves to next week) and a style (g gray, h personal/hatched, k protected, o task). The result line should agree with that array: the defaults (20 moved, 14 to next week, 12 clashes) are counted from it. Clash outlines stay red regardless of the accent colour.
